data.title: Debt collection "enforcement announcement" – Glücksmuster Premium
data.summary: ZFB Zentrale Forderungsbeitreibung s.r.o., a Slovak collection agency, demands €268.70 by 11 April 2025 for an online subscription "Glücksmuster Premium". It threatens a enforcement order, wage garnishment and credit bureau entries. The letter shows several scam indicators.
data.explanation: This is a private debt collection letter, not a court or authority document. It demands €268.70 within 4 days and says objections will no longer be handled, which is pressure and has no legal basis. A real enforcement order (Vollstreckungsbescheid) can only come from a court after a court payment order (Mahnbescheid), and you could object to that. Do not pay to the private account yet. Check whether you ever had this subscription and whether you received earlier reminders. Consider objecting to the claim in writing and ask for proof of the contract. A consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) can help check it.

key_facts.label: Reminder and collection costs (Mahn- und Inkassokosten)

warnings: Payee IBAN is Slovak and belongs to a private person (R. Horváth) on a 'Sonderkonto', not to the agency or the creditor.
Only 4 days to pay, with the statement that objections will no longer be handled, is typical pressure used in scam letters.
The letter is titled 'Vollstreckungsankündigung' and threatens an enforcement order, but no court payment order is mentioned; only a court can issue one.
Collection costs of €118.80 on a €149.90 claim look excessive, and the salutation 'Sehr geehrter Schuldner' is generic.
Do not transfer money before verifying the claim and the agency, for example with a consumer advice centre.
